entries.title: Malachi 2:1
segments:
This commandment; this charge to the priests with the accompanying rebukes. 
 
vv 1-9. 
 
A solemn responsibility rests upon religious teachers and rulers. Their opportunities to do good or evil are great.  If faithful to their Master and the souls of men, they may turn many from iniquity; but if unfaithful, they will corrupt God's worship, and cause many to stumble into perdition.  God will call them to account for their stewardship: if they have been true to their charge, he will honor them before all; but if they have betrayed his cause, and thus destroyed the souls of their fellow men, he will make them contemptible and base in this world and in that which is to come.

entries.title: Malachi 2:3
segments: Of your solemn feasts; that is, of the victims offered in your solemn feasts.  This is a clear intimation that all the services of these feasts were abominable to God, and should be rewarded with ignominy instead of honor.

entries.title: Malachi 2:4
segments: That my covenant might be with Levi; that it might be confirmed and faithfully observed on your part.  "Levi" stands here for the family of Levi.

entries.title: Malachi 2:5
segments: My covenant--of life and peace; there is a reference here to the promise made to Phinehas for his zeal in God's cause.

entries.title: Malachi 2:10
segments: Have we not all one father? the prophet proceeds to rebuke the sin of marrying foreign wives, which was connected with that of putting away wives of Hebrew origin.  Compare
.  He regards this, first, as a sin against the national covenant,

; secondly, as a sin against the repudiated Hebrew women. 
 
  Why do we deal treacherously--by profaning the covenant of our fathers? the marriage of foreign women was an act of treachery against God, and against the common brotherhood of the Jews, who were bound to help each other in sustaining the covenant made with their fathers.

entries.title: Malachi 2:11
segments: The Jews were forbidden to take wives from heathen nations, lest God's service should be corrupted by the intermixture of idolatrous rites; and the experience of all ages has shown that alliances of this kind are eminently disastrous to the cause of piety.  When believers unite themselves with those who reject Christ's gospel, they cannot reasonably hope for the blessing of a godly seed.

entries.title: Malachi 2:12
segments:
The master and the scholar; a proverbial expression, like "root and branch."  The reference is probably to the priests that kept watch in the temple, and answered to each other's call. 
 
  That offereth an offering; that is, while he allows himself in this sin.

entries.title: Malachi 2:13
segments: Again; perhaps with reference to the same sin committed under Ezra's administration.

But some render, "This again have ye done;" that is, to the sin of profaning my covenant, you have again added cruelty to your Hebrew wives, whom you have put away to make room for heathen wives. 
 
  Covering the altar; the altar at which the priests ministered is represented as covered with the tears and groans of the repudiated wives. 
 
vv 13-16. 
 
Polygamy and divorce are opposed alike to the original institution of marriage, to domestic peace and purity, and to the progress of true piety; wherever they prevail, they bring vice and misery in their train.

entries.title: Malachi 2:15
segments: Make one; that is, "one flesh," by the union of one man with one woman.  The prophet refers to the original institution of marriage, which alike excluded polygamy and divorce.

The residue of the spirit; the creative power remained with him, and he could have made more women had he seen good. 
 
  A godly seed; the design of the marriage institution, as originally established, is here given.

entries.title: Malachi 2:16
segments: Covereth violence with his garment; that is, cloaks his violence towards his wife under various pretences.  But some render, "heapeth violence upon his garment," garment being taken figuratively for wife.

entries.title: Malachi 2:17
segments: Every one that doeth evil--where is the God of judgment? see note on

. 
 
The present prosperity of the wicked has been in all ages a trial to the faith of God's people; but no true believer will allow himself to be seduced by it into the ways of sin; it is only they who have no faith in "the God of judgment," that will join themselves to the side of evil-doers.
